title: Minimum Increments to Equalize Leaf Paths
summary: Given an integer n and a tree with n nodes, where each node has a cost, the task is to equalize the scores of all root-to-leaf paths by increasing the cost of some nodes.
statement: Given an integer n and a tree with n nodes, where each node has a cost, the task is to equalize the scores of all root-to-leaf paths by increasing the cost of some nodes. The score of a path is the sum of the costs of the nodes along it. The goal is to find the minimum number of nodes whose cost must be increased to achieve this.
constraints: The positive-cost tree has up to 100,000 nodes and is rooted at zero.
Increase chosen node costs by arbitrary nonnegative amounts.
Minimize how many nodes are increased so every root-to-leaf path has equal total cost.
hints: At a node, every lower child-subtree maximum must be raised to the largest child maximum, and one increment at that child root raises all its leaf paths together.
Process bottom-up, returning the common node-to-leaf score and counting each deficient child branch once.
Set target=max(child scores), add the number below target, and return cost[node]+target.
Increasing the deficient child root is sufficient with one changed node, while any solution must change at least one node inside each independently deficient branch.
editorial: Increasing the deficient child root is sufficient with one changed node, while any solution must change at least one node inside each independently deficient branch.

tests.explanation: Raise node one by two so both root-to-leaf scores become five; one node changes.
There is only one root-to-leaf path, so no increment is needed.
